$comment: The registry of every diagnostic code pkinative reports. The diagnostics-parity rule of scripts/verify-docs.ts keeps it in bidirectional sync with the PkiDiagnosticCode union of src/types/pki-types.ts and requires a payload factory for every code in src/core/pki-diagnostics.ts. The union is additions-only: a code is never renamed or removed. Delivery: strict: true throws PKI_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC; onDiagnostic receives every diagnostic; otherwise console.warn once per code per operation. Parse results also record every diagnostic.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A serial number is longer than 20 octets.
diagnostics.remedy: Accept or refuse by policy; some verifiers refuse such certificates.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A serial number is zero or negative.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is still returned as decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The outer signatureAlgorithm differs from tbsCertificate.signature.
diagnostics.remedy: Treat the certificate as unverifiable; a verifier must refuse it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 algorithm identifier has absent or non-NULL parameters.
diagnostics.remedy: Accept or refuse by policy; RFC 3279 requires NULL parameters.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A certificate carries extensions but declares version 1 or 2.
diagnostics.remedy: The extensions are still decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A certificate carries a unique identifier but declares version 1.
diagnostics.remedy: The identifier is still decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A validity date before 2050 is encoded as a GeneralizedTime.
diagnostics.remedy: The instant is decoded correctly; the issuer violates the RFC 5280 encoding rule.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A GeneralizedTime in a certificate carries fractional seconds.
diagnostics.remedy: The instant is decoded to the millisecond; RFC 5280 forbids fractions in certificates.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: notBefore is later than notAfter.
diagnostics.remedy: The certificate is valid at no instant; refuse it wherever validity matters.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The issuer name is an empty sequence.
diagnostics.remedy: Chain building by name will not find an issuer; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The subject is empty and subjectAltName is absent or not critical.
diagnostics.remedy: Read the identity from subjectAltName, and treat the certificate as non-conforming.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A subjectAltName or issuerAltName extension contains no GeneralName.
diagnostics.remedy: The extension carries no identity; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A multi-valued relative distinguished name is not in DER SET OF order.
diagnostics.remedy: Compare names attribute by attribute, never by bytes.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A PrintableString contains an ASCII character outside the PrintableString alphabet, such as '*', '@' or '&'.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded as ASCII; web PKI issuers commonly do this in wildcard names.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A TeletexString is decoded.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded as ISO 8859-1, the interpretation of real-world issuers; read the raw bytes when T.61 semantics matter.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A critical extension has an OID pkinative does not decode.
diagnostics.remedy: A verifier must refuse the certificate unless it processes the extension itself (the raw value is kept).

diagnostics.raisedWhen: basicConstraints sets pathLenConstraint while cA is false.
diagnostics.remedy: Ignore the constraint; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: keyUsage asserts no bit.
diagnostics.remedy: Treat the key as usable for nothing; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A named bit list, such as keyUsage, keeps trailing zero bits.
diagnostics.remedy: The bits decode identically; the encoder is not DER.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: nameConstraints is not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: Enforce the constraints anyway; RFC 5280 requires conforming CAs to mark them critical.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: nameConstraints appears in a certificate whose basicConstraints does not assert cA.
diagnostics.remedy: Ignore the constraints: the extension MUST be used only in a CA certificate, and an end-entity certificate issues nothing for it to constrain. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: basicConstraints asserts cA without being marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative reads the extension whatever its criticality, which is the safe direction; a verifier that skipped non-critical extensions would not see that this is a CA. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: policyConstraints is present and not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative enforces it anyway; a verifier that ignored it would grant a path the policy the CA withheld. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: keyUsage asserts keyCertSign while basicConstraints does not assert cA.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing to do: RFC 5280 §6.1.4 (k) refuses to let a certificate without cA issue anything, whatever its keyUsage says. The bit is for CA certificates only and the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A v3 certificate that names another subject as its issuer carries no authorityKeyIdentifier.
diagnostics.remedy: Build the path by issuer name instead, trying every candidate whose subject matches: buildCertificatePath already does, so this costs exploration rather than correctness. When you are the issuer, computeKeyIdentifier over your own key bits and encodeAuthorityKeyIdentifier write it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A v3 certificate asserting cA carries no subjectKeyIdentifier.
diagnostics.remedy: Certificates this CA issues cannot name its key, so their authorityKeyIdentifier will match nothing and path building falls back to names. computeKeyIdentifier over the CA public key bits and encodeSubjectKeyIdentifier write it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The subject carries a commonName that is not one of the subjectAltName entries, and the certificate has a subjectAltName.
diagnostics.remedy: Match the host against subjectAltName only, which is what checkServerName does whenever a SAN names a host. A name appearing only in the commonName is one no modern relying party will match, and CA/Browser Forum BR 7.1.4.3 forbids issuing it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A dNSName in subjectAltName or issuerAltName falls outside RFC 1034's preferred name syntax — an empty label, a leading or trailing dot, or a character outside letters, digits and hyphen.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is compared literally, so it can only ever match a host asked for with the same spelling; nothing silently normalises it. Underscores are common in practice and resolve in DNS, which is why this is a diagnostic and not a refusal.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A dNSName, rfc822Name or uniformResourceIdentifier holds a NUL, another C0 control (U+0000 to U+001F) or DEL. IA5String admits them; no name syntax does.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is kept and compared literally, so a.example�.evil.example never matches a.example. A display, log or C consumer that stops at NUL would read a different name than the one compared (the CVE-2009-2408 class): escape the value before showing it, and treat the certificate as suspect.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: authorityKeyIdentifier carries only one of authorityCertIssuer and authorityCertSerialNumber.
diagnostics.remedy: Use keyIdentifier for chain building; the pair is unusable alone.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: certificatePolicies lists one policy OID more than once.
diagnostics.remedy: Every occurrence is kept as decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: policyConstraints sets neither requireExplicitPolicy nor inhibitPolicyMapping.
diagnostics.remedy: The extension constrains nothing; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A field with a DEFAULT value carries that value explicitly: version v1, critical FALSE, cA FALSE, a subtree minimum of 0.
diagnostics.remedy: Every reader decodes the same value, so the certificate is read as encoded (as Go, OpenSSL and BoringSSL read it); pass strict: true to refuse encoders that are not DER.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: encodingRules is 'ber' and the input uses a construct DER forbids (indefinite length, constructed string, non-minimal length, a non-canonical BOOLEAN).
diagnostics.remedy: Expected for BER inputs such as CMS; never re-sign or compare such bytes as if they were DER.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: mode is 'lax' and a block deviates from the strict grammar: whitespace around a boundary line or inside the base64 text, base64 lines that are not 64 characters long, or RFC 1421 headers. Explanatory text outside blocks is ignored in both modes, as RFC 7468 §2 requires.
diagnostics.remedy: Expected for hand-edited or legacy PEM; fix the producer to get strict output.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A SignedData or SignerInfo declares a version RFC 5652 defines, but not the one §5.1 or §5.3 derives from what it carries — for instance a SignedData declaring 1 while a signer uses subjectKeyIdentifier, which calls for 3.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing to do as a verifier: the version is not signed and decides nothing, and RFC 5652 §1.3 asks readers to be forgiving of it. Report it to the producer, since a strict reader may refuse the message.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: One of the SET OF fields that no signature covers — digestAlgorithms, certificates, crls or signerInfos — is not in DER order (X.690 §11.6). Common: 91 of the 224 signed messages in NIST PKITS carry an unsorted certificate set.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing signed depends on the order, so verification is unaffected. Report it to the producer if the message must pass a strict DER reader.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A signer's signed attributes are not in DER SET OF order, which RFC 5652 §5.3 requires. The signature is verified over the bytes as they were signed, not over a re-sorted set.
diagnostics.remedy: The signature may be perfectly good. Expect other verifiers — those that re-encode the set before checking the signature — to reject it, and report it to the producer.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A signer uses a digest algorithm that SignedData.digestAlgorithms does not list. The list lets a one-pass verifier start hashing the content before it reaches the signers.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative is not a one-pass verifier and is unaffected. RFC 5652 §5.1 lets such a verifier fail the message, so report it to the producer.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A PBKDF2 iteration count, for a key, a bag of certificates or a PBMAC1 MAC, is below the 1 000 RFC 8018 recommends. The file still opens.
diagnostics.remedy: The count sets what a stolen copy of the file costs to brute-force. Re-export it with a higher one — OpenSSL 3 writes 2 048 by default, and OWASP recommends 600 000 for PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA-256.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A CRL's cRLNumber or deltaCRLIndicator is not a DER INTEGER, or an entry's reasonCode is not a CRLReason value RFC 5280 assigns or its invalidityDate is not a GeneralizedTime. The value is ignored: none of them decides whether a serial is revoked, and a delta whose base number cannot be read is never paired with a base.
diagnostics.remedy: Report it to the CA that issued the list. A revocation with an unreadable reason is still a revocation; a delta with an unreadable base number answers nothing until the CA reissues it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A name attribute RFC 5280 Appendix A.1 defines is encoded outside its syntax: countryName, serialNumber or dnQualifier not a PrintableString, domainComponent or emailAddress not an IA5String, or a DirectoryString attribute (commonName, organizationName, …) as none of TeletexString, PrintableString, UniversalString, UTF8String and BMPString.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is still decoded and names still compare by their bytes; a strict reader (pkilint, zlint) refuses the name, so have the issuer re-encode it — pkinative's encodeNameAttribute writes the defined type by default.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A countryName value is not exactly two characters (X520countryName ::= PrintableString (SIZE (2))).
diagnostics.remedy: The value is still decoded; the issuer should write the ISO 3166 alpha-2 code. encodeNameAttribute refuses any other length.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A name attribute value is longer, in characters, than the upper bound RFC 5280 Appendix A.1 gives its type (X.520 ub-*): commonName, organizationName, organizationalUnitName, title and serialNumber 64, localityName, stateOrProvinceName and pseudonym 128, emailAddress 255, name, surname, givenName, initials and generationQualifier 32768 (ub-name); dnQualifier and domainComponent are unbounded, and a countryName of the wrong size is PKI_DIAG_COUNTRY_NAME_SIZE.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is read as it is and names still compare by their bytes; a reader that enforces the SIZE constraint refuses the name, so have the issuer shorten the value — encodeNameAttribute refuses one past the bound when writing.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A two-letter countryName is not an officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code — UK, EU, a formerly assigned code such as AN, or lower-case letters — and not in the user-assigned range AA, QM–QZ, XA–XZ, ZZ (ISO 3166-1 §8.1.3), which is admitted silently.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is read as it is. ISO 3166-1 assigns codes over time, so an unknown one is for the relying party to judge; an issuer should write the assigned code (GB, not UK) in capitals.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A BMPString or UniversalString starts with the byte-order signature U+FEFF (X.690: "Signatures shall not be used").
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded with the U+FEFF kept, so it compares unequal to the same text without it; the issuer should drop the signature.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A UTF8String, BMPString or UniversalString contains an ISO/IEC 2022 code-extension control (ESC, SO, SI, SS2 or SS3), which X.690 forbids in the ISO/IEC 10646 string types.
diagnostics.remedy: The value is decoded as ISO/IEC 10646 regardless; a reader that honours the escape shows other characters, so treat the text with suspicion and have the issuer re-encode it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A subjectDirectoryAttributes extension is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The attributes are still decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process the extension must refuse the certificate.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An RSA SubjectPublicKeyInfo carries a public exponent below 3 or an even one, outside the RSA RFC 8017 §3.1 defines. Under e = 1 a message is its own signature, so anyone can sign for the key; Web Crypto imports such a key regardless.
diagnostics.remedy: The key decodes and the certificate parses, but no signature under this key is checked: verification reports PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_NOT_CHECKED with PKI_CRYPTO_KEY_UNSUPPORTED. The certificate has to be reissued for a proper key.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An EC SubjectPublicKeyInfo does not name a curve pkinative knows: its parameters are NULL (implicitCurve) or explicit curve parameters (specifiedCurve), both of which RFC 5480 §2.1.1 forbids, or a namedCurve OID other than P-256, P-384 and P-521.
diagnostics.remedy: The key decodes with curve undefined and the certificate parses, but no signature under this key is checked: verification reports PKI_REASON_SIGNATURE_NOT_CHECKED with PKI_CRYPTO_KEY_UNSUPPORTED. Reissue the certificate with a namedCurve on a curve Web Crypto supports.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A certificate carries an issuerUniqueID or a subjectUniqueID, whatever its version.
diagnostics.remedy: The identifiers are decoded and given no meaning; RFC 5280 forbids conforming CAs to generate them. Issue without them.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: authorityKeyIdentifier is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The identifier is read either way; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process the extension must refuse the certificate.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: subjectKeyIdentifier is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The identifier is read either way; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process the extension must refuse the certificate.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A v3 certificate that does not assert cA carries no subjectKeyIdentifier.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused. RFC 5280 recommends the identifier; the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements now advise against it in subscriber certificates, so decide by the profile you issue under.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: keyUsage is present and not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative enforces keyUsage either way; a verifier that skipped non-critical extensions would not. Mark it critical when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The anyPolicy entry of certificatePolicies carries a qualifier other than a CPS pointer or a user notice.
diagnostics.remedy: The qualifier is kept undecoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280. Use only the CPS pointer and user notice qualifiers with anyPolicy.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A user notice qualifier carries a noticeRef.
diagnostics.remedy: The reference is decoded; few relying parties can resolve it to text, which is why RFC 5280 advises against it. Put the text in explicitText instead.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A user notice's explicitText is a VisibleString or a BMPString.
diagnostics.remedy: The text is decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280, which asks for UTF8String (IA5String is allowed). Encode it as UTF8String.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A user notice's explicitText contains a character from U+0000 to U+001F or from U+007F to U+009F.
diagnostics.remedy: The text is kept as decoded; strip control characters before displaying it, and leave them out when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A UTF8String explicitText changes under Unicode normalization form C.
diagnostics.remedy: The text is kept as decoded and compared as such; normalize it to NFC when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An issuerDomainPolicy of policyMappings is not one of the policy identifiers of the same certificate's certificatePolicies.
diagnostics.remedy: Path validation applies the mapping regardless; assert every mapped issuer-domain policy in certificatePolicies when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: policyMappings is present and not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative applies the mapping either way; mark it critical when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: subjectAltName is marked critical in a certificate whose subject is not empty.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; RFC 5280 reserves the critical flag for a certificate whose identity lives only in the extension. Mark it non-critical when the subject is set.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A uniformResourceIdentifier of subjectAltName or issuerAltName is not an RFC 3986 URI: a relative reference, a character the grammar does not allow in its place, or a bad percent-encoding.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is kept and compared literally; two URI parsers may read it differently, so do not derive a host from it. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A uniformResourceIdentifier of subjectAltName or issuerAltName has no scheme, or nothing after the scheme's colon.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is kept and compared literally; it names no resource. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A uniformResourceIdentifier of subjectAltName or issuerAltName has an authority whose host is neither a fully qualified domain name in preferred name syntax nor an IPv4 or bracketed IPv6 address.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is kept and compared literally; a URI name constraint cannot place its host. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: subjectAltName or issuerAltName holds an empty rfc822Name, dNSName, uniformResourceIdentifier, x400Address or ediPartyName, or a directoryName with no RDN.
diagnostics.remedy: The empty name is kept and matches nothing; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: issuerAltName is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; mark it non-critical when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A GeneralSubtree of nameConstraints sets a minimum other than 0, or any maximum.
diagnostics.remedy: Path validation never treats such a subtree as covering a name: a bounded permitted subtree permits nothing. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A uniformResourceIdentifier constraint of nameConstraints is not a fully qualified domain name, with or without one leading period.
diagnostics.remedy: The constraint is still applied to the host of each URI, as written; the issuer violates RFC 5280. Write a host, or a domain with a leading period.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: extKeyUsage is marked critical and lists anyExtendedKeyUsage.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; a critical extension that permits any purpose contradicts itself. Mark it non-critical when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: cRLDistributionPoints is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; mark it non-critical when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A DistributionPoint of cRLDistributionPoints or freshestCRL has neither distributionPoint nor cRLIssuer.
diagnostics.remedy: The point is decoded as written and locates no CRL by itself; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An ldap URI of a distribution point's fullName has no <dn>, or not exactly one non-empty <attrdesc>.
diagnostics.remedy: The URI is kept as written; an LDAP client cannot tell which entry and attribute hold the CRL. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A distribution point's name includes no http or ldap URI (an https URI is another scheme).
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; fetch the CRL by whatever the name offers, and offer an http or ldap URI when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A distribution point is named by nameRelativeToCRLIssuer.
diagnostics.remedy: The RDN is decoded; RFC 5280 advises against it. Use fullName when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A distribution point uses nameRelativeToCRLIssuer while its cRLIssuer holds more than one directoryName.
diagnostics.remedy: The name is relative to no one issuer; the issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: inhibitAnyPolicy is present and not marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: pkinative enforces it either way; a verifier that ignored it would accept anyPolicy the CA withheld. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: freshestCRL is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The points are decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process delta CRLs must refuse the certificate.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: authorityInfoAccess is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The descriptions are decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process the extension must refuse the certificate.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: subjectInfoAccess is marked critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The descriptions are decoded; the issuer violates RFC 5280, and a relying party that does not process the extension must refuse the certificate.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An ldap URI given as an id-ad-caIssuers location of authorityInfoAccess, or an id-ad-caRepository location of subjectInfoAccess, has no <dn> or no <attributes>; the path names the extension.
diagnostics.remedy: The URI is kept as written; an LDAP client cannot tell which entry and attributes hold the certificates. The issuer violates RFC 5280.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: authorityInfoAccess lists id-ad-caIssuers, and none of its locations is an http or ldap URI.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; fetch issuers by whatever the locations offer, and offer an http or ldap URI when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: subjectInfoAccess lists id-ad-caRepository, and none of its locations is an http or ldap URI.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused; offer an http or ldap URI when you issue.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A SignedData with no SignerInfo whose eContentType is not id-data, or which still carries an eContent — the certificates-only message of RFC 5652 §5.2 with a content it must not have.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is refused and there is no signer to judge; the certificates and CRLs are read as carried. Report it to the producer: a strict reader may refuse the message.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A countersignature (an unsigned attribute id-countersignature) whose own SignerInfo carries a content-type attribute among its signed attributes, which RFC 5652 §11.4 forbids: there is no content type for a countersignature.
diagnostics.remedy: The countersignature is carried, not verified, so nothing changes here; a verifier of the countersignature may refuse it. Report it to the countersigner.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A countersignature whose SignerInfo has signed attributes and no message-digest attribute among them, which RFC 5652 §11.4 requires whenever any other attribute is signed.
diagnostics.remedy: The countersignature is carried, not verified; one without a message-digest binds its signature to nothing a verifier can recompute. Report it to the countersigner.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A countersignature attribute whose SET OF values is empty; RFC 5652 §11.4 requires one or more SignerInfo values.
diagnostics.remedy: The attribute countersigns nothing and is kept as received, like any attribute with no value. Report it to the countersigner.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A signingTime attribute encoded as GeneralizedTime for a date between 1 January 1950 and 31 December 2049, which RFC 5652 §11.3 requires as UTCTime.
diagnostics.remedy: The instant is read as written and the signature is verified over the bytes as signed; a strict reader may refuse the attribute. Report it to the signer. createSignedData writes UTCTime for those years.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A GeneralizedTime signingTime attribute with fractional seconds, which RFC 5652 §11.3 forbids.
diagnostics.remedy: The instant is read to the millisecond and the signature is verified over the bytes as signed. Report it to the signer. createSignedData writes whole seconds.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: verifyTimeStampToken was given the request, the request set certReq TRUE, and the token carries no certificate, or certificates that do not include the TSA certificate that verified it (found among the certificates passed).
diagnostics.remedy: The verdict is unchanged: the TSA is found among the token certificates and the ones you pass. A reader given the token alone cannot find it; ask the TSA to honour certReq.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: verifyTimeStampToken was given the request, the request did not set certReq (FALSE or absent), and the token carries certificates anyway, which RFC 3161 §2.4.1 then forbids.
diagnostics.remedy: The verdict is unchanged: the certificates are read as the TSA hint they are. Ask the TSA to omit them, or set certReq in your requests.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A BasicOCSPResponse whose certs field is present and holds no certificate; RFC 6960 §4.2.1 says the field should then be absent.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing is lost: the responder is looked for exactly as if the field were absent. Advice to the responder.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A ResponseData whose explicit version is not the one-octet INTEGER 0 of v1 — another value, or not an INTEGER. RFC 6960 §4.2.2.3 defines v1 alone. An explicit v1 is PKI_DIAG_DEFAULT_ENCODED instead.
diagnostics.remedy: The response is read with the v1 syntax, the only one there is; a strict reader may refuse it. Report it to the responder.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: checkOcspStatus was given the signer certificate and the responderID names neither its subject (byName) nor the SHA-1 of its public key bits (byKey); RFC 6960 §4.2.2.3 requires the two to correspond. verifyCertificateChain passes the certificate that both signed the response and was entitled to.
diagnostics.remedy: The verdict is unchanged: the signature decides who answered, and the responderID is what the responder claims about itself. Report it to the responder.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The response carries SingleResponse elements about certificates other than the one asked about, beside the answer about it; RFC 6960 §4.2.2.3 says a responder should not add them, and allows pre-generated responses (RFC 5019 §2.2.1) to.
diagnostics.remedy: Nothing to do: the answer about the certificate asked about is the one judged, found by all three CertID fields, never by position.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: checkOcspStatus was given the signer certificate and it marks id-pkix-ocsp-nocheck critical; RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2.1 says the extension should be non-critical.
diagnostics.remedy: The extension is honoured either way; a reader that does not know it must refuse the certificate. Advice to the CA that issued the responder certificate.
